electronegativityDescription: Electronegativity is a tool to identify misconfigurations and security anti-patterns in Electron applications.
inputOptionDescription: input: a directory, .js, .html, .asar, an installed app's folder or executable, or an installer or package (NSIS or Squirrel .exe, .7z, .zip, .nupkg)
checksOptionDescription: only run the specified checks list, passed in csv format
excludeChecksOptionDescription: skip the specified checks list, passed in csv format
severityOptionDescription: only return findings with the specified level of severity or above
confidenceOptionDescription: only return findings with the specified level of confidence or above
outputOptionDescription: save the results to a file: .html report, .json, .sarif, .csv, .docx (Word report) or .cdx.json (CycloneDX SBOM); several separated by commas
verboseOptionDescription: show the description for the findings, defaults to true
electronVersionOptionDescription: assume the set Electron version, overriding the detected one, eg -e 7.0.0 to treat as using Electron 7
parserPluginsOptionDescription: specify additional parser plugins to use separated by commas, e.g. -p optionalChaining
tryElectroNgShort: Need something more powerful or updated? Try ElectroNG at get-electrong.com...
contactUs: Have a question? Contact us at: info@doyensec.com
foundBug: Found a bug? Please open an issue: https://github.com/doyensec/electronegativity/issues
fileFormatError: Please use an output file ending in .html, .json, .sarif or .csv.
electronVersionError: Couldn't detect Electron version, assuming v0.1.0. Defaults have probably changed for your actual version, please check manually.
severityLevelError: This severity level does not exist!
confidenceLevelError: This confidence level does not exist!
tryElectroNg: Tip: save a filterable HTML report with -o report.html (or .json, .sarif, .csv).
BROWSER_WINDOW_WEB_PREFERENCES_DEPRECATI: (ELECTRON 5) The BrowserWindow API's webPreferences option default values are deprecated in favor of the new defaults.
NATIVE_WINDOW_OPEN_CHANGE: (ELECTRON 5) Child windows opened with the nativeWindowOpen option will always have Node.js integration disabled.
PRIVILEGED_SCHEMES_REGISTRATION_REMOVAL: (ELECTRON 5) The APIs for Privileged Schemes Registration have been removed in favor of protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged.
SET_SPELLCHECK_PROVIDER_DEPRECATION: (ELECTRON 5) The spellCheck callback on webFrame.setSpellCheckProvider is now asynchronous, and autoCorrectWord parameter has been removed.
WEB_FRAME_ISOLATED_WORLD_DEPRECATION: (ELECTRON 5) The webFrame isolated world APIs have been deprecated in favor of webFrame.setIsolatedWorldInfo
CONTENT_TRACING_GET_TRACE_BUFFER_USAGE_D: (ELECTRON 6) Calling contentTracing.getTraceBufferUsage() with a callback is deprecated.
ENABLE_MIXED_SANDBOX_DEPRECATION: (ELECTRON 6) The app.enableMixedSandbox API has been deprecated since mixed-sandbox mode is now enabled by default.
QUERY_SYSTEM_IDLE_STATE_DEPRECATION: (ELECTRON 6) The powerMonitor.querySystemIdleState API has been deprecated.
QUERY_SYSTEM_IDLE_TIME_DEPRECATION: (ELECTRON 6) The powerMonitor.querySystemIdleTime API has been deprecated.
REQUIRE_ELECTRON_SCREEN_DEPRECATION: (ELECTRON 6) require('electron').screen in the renderer process is deprecated.
REQUIRE_SANDBOXED_RENDERERS_DEPRECATION: (ELECTRON 6) Certain requires in sandboxed renderers are deprecated.
SET_HIGHLIGHT_MODE_DEPRECATION: (ELECTRON 6) The tray.setHighlightMode API has been deprecated.
SET_NULL_MENU_DEPRECATION: (ELECTRON 6) Calling win.setMenu(null) to remove a menu has been deprecated in favor of win.removeMenu().
CLEAR_AUTH_CACHE_DEPRECATION: (ELECTRON 7) The session.clearAuthCache API no longer accepts options for what to clear, and instead unconditionally clears the whole cache.
CONTENT_TRACING_GET_TRACE_BUFFER_USAGE_R: (ELECTRON 7) Calling contentTracing.getTraceBufferUsage() with a callback has been removed.
ENABLE_MIXED_SANDBOX_REMOVAL: (ELECTRON 7) The app.enableMixedSandbox API has been removed since mixed-sandbox mode is now enabled by default.
QUERY_SYSTEM_IDLE_STATE_REMOVAL: (ELECTRON 7) The powerMonitor.querySystemIdleState API has been replaced with the synchronous API powerMonitor.getSystemIdleState.
QUERY_SYSTEM_IDLE_TIME_REMOVAL: (ELECTRON 7) The powerMonitor.querySystemIdleTime API has been replaced with the synchronous API powerMonitor.getSystemIdleTime.
SET_HIGHLIGHT_MODE_REMOVAL: (ELECTRON 7) The tray.setHighlightMode API has been removed.
WEB_FRAME_ISOLATED_WORLD_REMOVAL: (ELECTRON 7) The webFrame isolated world APIs have been removed in favor of webFrame.setIsolatedWorldInfo
WEBKITDIRECTORY_CHANGE: Fixed webkitdirectory to return list of files if a folder is selected.
ALLOW_RENDERER_PROCESS_REUSE_DEPRECATION: (ELECTRON 8) The default value of false for app.allowRendererProcessReuse is deprecated
GET_COLOR_DEPRECATION: (ELECTRON 8) The color alternate-selected-control-text on systemPreferences.getColor(color) is deprecated
GET_WEB_CONTENTS_DEPRECATION: (ELECTRON 8) getWebContents is deprecated on the <webview> tag.
IPC_SEND_STRUCTURED_CLONE_ALGORITHM: (ELECTRON 8) Values sent over IPC are now serialized with Structured Clone Algorithm.
SET_ZOOM_LEVEL_LIMITS_DEPRECATION: (ELECTRON 8) setLayoutZoomLevelLimits is deprecated on webContents, webFrame, and the <webview> tag because Chromium removed this capability.
VISIBLE_ON_FULLSCREEN_DEPRECATION: (ELECTRON 8) The option visibleOnFullScreen on BrowserWindow.setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces is deprecated
AFFINITY_HTML_CHECK: Review the use of affinity property
AFFINITY_JS_CHECK: Review the use of affinity property
ALLOWPOPUPS_HTML_CHECK: Do not allow popups in webview
AUXCLICK_HTML_CHECK: Limit navigation flows to untrusted origins. Middle-click may cause Electron to open a link within a new window
AUXCLICK_JS_CHECK: Limit navigation flows to untrusted origins. Middle-click may cause Electron to open a link within a new window
BLINK_FEATURES_HTML_CHECK: Do not use Chromium's experimental features
BLINK_FEATURES_JS_CHECK: Do not use Chromium’s experimental features
CERTIFICATE_ERROR_EVENT_JS_CHECK: Do not allow insecure connections, by explicitly opting-out from TLS validation
CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_PROC_JS_CHECK: Do not allow insecure connections, by explicitly opting-out from TLS validation or importing untrusted certificates
CONTEXT_ISOLATION_JS_CHECK: Review the use of the contextIsolation option
CSP_HTML_CHECK: A CSP is set for this page using a meta tag
CSP_JS_CHECK: Check for common responseHeaders CSP assignments
CUSTOM_ARGUMENTS_JS_CHECK: Review the use of custom command line arguments
CUSTOM_ARGUMENTS_JSON_CHECK: Search for dangerous runtime flags in the package.json file.
DANGEROUS_FUNCTIONS_JS_CHECK: Do not use insertCSS, executeJavaScript, eval, Function, setTimeout, setInterval, setImmediate with user-supplied content
ELECTRON_VERSION_JSON_CHECK: Gets the electron version used by inspecting the package.json file.
EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURES_HTML_CHECK: Do not use Chromium's experimental features
EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURES_JS_CHECK: Do not use Chromium's experimental features
HTTP_RESOURCES_HTML_CHECK: Do not allow insecure HTTP connections
HTTP_RESOURCES_JS_CHECK: Do not allow insecure HTTP connections
INSECURE_CONTENT_HTML_CHECK: Do not allow insecure HTTP connections
INSECURE_CONTENT_JS_CHECK: Do not allow insecure HTTP connections
LIMIT_NAVIGATION_JS_CHECK: Evaluate the implementation of the navigation limits (will-navigate, will-frame-navigate, setWindowOpenHandler)
PRELOAD_JS_CHECK: Review the use of preload scripts
PROTOCOL_HANDLER_JS_CHECK: Review the use of custom protocol handlers
SECURITY_WARNINGS_DISABLED_JS_CHECK: Warns about flags disabling security warnings in the sources.
SECURITY_WARNINGS_DISABLED_JSON_CHECK: Warns about flags disabling security warnings in the package.json file.
AFFINITY_GLOBAL_CHECK_AFFINITY_FOUND: Two or more rendereres are running with the same affinity property. Manual review is required since we don't check for the webPreferences.
ALLOW_RENDERER_PROCESS_REUSE_GLOBAL_DEPR: (ELECTRON 8) The default value of app.allowRendererProcessReuse is deprecated, it is currently false.  It will changed to be true in Electron 9.
AVAILABLE_SECURITY_FIXES_GLOBAL_CHECK_SE: The Electron version in use is affected by published security advisories that are fixed in newer releases
AVAILABLE_SECURITY_FIXES_GLOBAL_CHECK_OU: A newer patch release of the Electron version in use is available
CSP_GLOBAL_CHECK_NO_CSP: No CSP has been detected in the target application
CSP_GLOBAL_CHECK_MAYBE_WEAK_CSP: One or more CSP directives detected seems to be vulnerable
CSP_GLOBAL_CHECK_WEAK_CSP: One or more CSP directives detected are vulnerable
CSP_GLOBAL_CHECK_INVALID_CSP: Failed to parse CSP, it may not be valid.
HTTP_RESOURCES_WITH_NODE_INTEGRATION_GLO: The nodeIntegration flag is enabled for the application, but some resources are loaded over an unencrypted connection.
LIMIT_NAVIGATION_GLOBAL_CHECK_NONE_FOUND: Missing navigation limits: no will-navigate handler and no setWindowOpenHandler
PERMISSION_REQUEST_HANDLER_GLOBAL_CHECK: Missing PermissionRequestHandler to limit specific permissions (e.g. openExternal) in response to events from particular origins.
IPC_SENDER_VALIDATION_JS_CHECK: IPC handler does not appear to validate the sender (event.senderFrame) before acting on the message
CONTEXT_BRIDGE_EXPOSURE_JS_CHECK: Powerful Electron/Node.js APIs are exposed to the renderer through contextBridge
FUSES_GLOBAL_CHECK: No Electron Fuses configuration found. RunAsNode, NODE_OPTIONS, --inspect and ASAR integrity fuses are insecure by default
WINDOW_OPEN_HANDLER_JS_CHECK: setWindowOpenHandler allows new windows to be created; verify that only trusted URLs are allowed
WEBVIEW_TAG_JS_CHECK_WILL_ATTACH: A will-attach-webview handler is registered; verify that it strips preload scripts and enforces secure webPreferences
WEBVIEW_GLOBAL_CHECK: The <webview> tag is enabled but no will-attach-webview handler verifies webview options before creation
DEVTOOLS_JS_CHECK: DevTools are opened programmatically; ensure this cannot happen in production builds
PROTOCOL_PRIVILEGES_JS_CHECK: Custom scheme registered with risky privileges
NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED_JS_CHECK: TLS certificate validation is disabled for Node.js connections (NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 or rejectUnauthorized: false)
OPEN_PATH_JS_CHECK: Review the use of shell.openPath with non-constant paths: opening attacker-influenced paths can execute files
SHOWITEMINFOLDER_JS_CHECK: Review the use of shell.showItemInFolder with non-constant paths
WRITE_SHORTCUT_JS_CHECK: Review the use of shell.writeShortcutLink: attacker-influenced shortcuts can point to arbitrary executables
FILE_HANDLER_JS_CHECK: Validate untrusted input received by the main process
FILE_HANDLER_JSON_CHECK: The application registers file associations or URL schemes; their handlers receive untrusted input
SECUREKEYBOARDENTRY_JS_CHECK: Review the use of Secure Keyboard Entry (macOS)
SECUREKEYBOARDENTRY_GLOBAL_CHECK: Password fields are used but Secure Keyboard Entry is never enabled on macOS (app.setSecureKeyboardEntryEnabled(true))
WEBGL_JS_CHECK: WebGL is explicitly enabled; disable it if the renderer doesn't need it to reduce the attack surface
WEBSQL_JS_CHECK: WebSQL is explicitly enabled; disable it to reduce the attack surface
CERTIFICATE_PINNING_GLOBAL_CHECK: No certificate pinning found (session.setCertificateVerifyProc); consider pinning the certificates of the backends the application trusts
LIMIT_NAVIGATION_JS_CHECK_NEW_WINDOW_REM: The 'new-window' event was removed in Electron 22 and no longer limits the creation of new windows; use setWindowOpenHandler
UNSUPPORTED_VERSION_GLOBAL_CHECK_END_OF_: The Electron version in use is no longer supported and does not receive security fixes
offlineOptionDescription: skip the checks that need network access (Electron releases and security advisories)
FILE_PROTOCOL_JS_CHECK: Local content is loaded over file://, which has extra privileges in Electron; prefer a custom protocol (protocol.handle)
UNTRUSTED_LOAD_URL_JS_CHECK: An app window loads a URL provided by untrusted input
IFRAME_SANDBOX_CHECK: Sandbox iframes that display documents or untrusted content: an unsandboxed frame can script the embedding page and reach its preload APIs or, with nodeIntegration, Node.js
XSS_SINK_JS_CHECK: HTML is built from dynamic data; unsanitized input leads to XSS in the renderer
COMMAND_INJECTION_JS_CHECK: A child process is started with a dynamic command
NAVIGATE_ON_DRAG_DROP_JS_CHECK: Dropping a file or link onto the window navigates to it
SANDBOX_JS_CHECK_ENABLED_GLOBALLY: app.enableSandbox() sandboxes every renderer, regardless of webPreferences.sandbox
PRELOAD_JS_CHECK_ISOLATED: Preload script with context isolation; what it exposes through contextBridge is analyzed by CONTEXT_BRIDGE_EXPOSURE_JS_CHECK
allFilesOptionDescription: also scan tests, fixtures, vendored and minified files (skipped by default)
baselineOptionDescription: don't report the findings accepted in this baseline file
writeBaselineOptionDescription: write the current findings to a baseline file (reasons already recorded are kept)
failOnOptionDescription: exit with code 1 when a reported finding has this severity or higher (high, medium, low, informational)
baselineSummary: {{suppressed}} finding(s) accepted by the baseline were not reported; {{stale}} baseline entry(ies) no longer match anything
PLAINTEXT_SECRETS_JS_CHECK: A secret is stored without encryption
ANGULAR_SCE_DISABLED_JS_CHECK: AngularJS Strict Contextual Escaping ($sce) is disabled for the whole application
ANGULAR_RESOURCE_URL_LIST_JS_CHECK: The AngularJS resource URL allowlist lets templates load from untrusted locations
ANGULAR_TRUST_HTML_JS_CHECK: AngularJS trusts or compiles dynamic markup ($sce.trustAsHtml, $compile), bypassing escaping
RICH_TEXT_EDITOR_JS_CHECK: HTML is loaded into a rich-text editor; sanitize it on the server, not only in the editor
SANITIZER_CONFIG_JS_CHECK: An HTML sanitizer or rich-text editor is configured to let script-bearing markup through
ANGULAR_BIND_HTML_UNSAFE_HTML_CHECK: ng-bind-html-unsafe renders its expression as raw HTML with no escaping
END_OF_LIFE_LIBRARY_GLOBAL_CHECK: Library version that no longer receives security fixes
GLOBAL_EXPOSURE_JS_CHECK: Global object exposed by an assignment
watchOptionDescription: run the app (its folder, packaged executable or .app bundle) and report what happens while you use it; close the app when done
watchArgsOptionDescription: extra command line arguments for the app started by --watch
watchLogOptionDescription: analyze the log of an earlier --watch session instead of starting the app
watchMarkerOptionDescription: a unique marker token to detect stored-content injection: plant content carrying it (e.g. x) and watch mode reports if it comes back as live HTML in another view
watchStarting: Starting the app in watch mode: log in and go through the features you want covered, then close the app (or press Ctrl+C here).
watchLogSaved: Session log saved to {{{file}}} (reuse it with --watch-log)
watchNoHook: The app did not load the watch mode observer, so nothing was observed. A packaged app loads it through the Node inspector, which builds with the EnableNodeCliInspectArguments fuse off don't allow: use a test build with that fuse on, or run the app folder with Electron installed. The diagnostics file (--diagnostics) records what went wrong.
watchInspectFuseOff: This build has the EnableNodeCliInspectArguments fuse off, so the watch mode observer can't be loaded into it and the session would record nothing. Use a test build with that fuse on (the static scan still covers the app's code).
watchNoWindows: The app opened no windows during this session, so there is nothing to report for it. Usually another copy of the app was still running (check the tray and Task Manager, close it, then run the session again), or the app closed on its own.
watchFusesUnreadable: No Electron fuse configuration was found in {{{file}}}, so the fuses of the packaged app could not be checked
watchCaptureOptionDescription: in watch mode, do not download the scripts and templates pages load for the static scan
remoteOptionDescription: also scan the front end served at this URL (its page, scripts, source maps and templates); can be repeated
remoteHeaderOptionDescription: header sent with --remote and watch-capture requests to the same site, e.g. "Cookie: session=..." for a test account; can be repeated
remoteFetching: Downloading the front-end code served remotely...
remoteOffline: --remote needs network access: nothing was downloaded, as --offline is set
remoteScanning: Scanning {{count}} front-end files served remotely (saved in {{{dir}}})
appOptionDescription: guided run: find the app in this install folder (or its executable), scan it, then walk through watch sessions, writing every report to one results folder
outOptionDescription: results folder for --app (default: electronegativity-results-<date> in the current folder)
sessionsOptionDescription: number of watch sessions --app runs without asking (0 for the static scan only)
appNoExecutable: No executable was found next to the app's code, so only the static scan runs. Point --app at the app's executable to run watch sessions.
appStatic: Scanning the app's code (all of it, including what is behind the login)...
appMarker: Planted-content marker for this run: {{marker}}. As one account, put it into content others will see (for example a document's text); as another account, open that content.
appAskFirstSession: Start watch session {{n}}? The app opens: log in, go through its features, then close it completely. [Enter = start, s = skip]
appAskNextSession: Start watch session {{n}} (for example as a second account)? [Enter = start, s = finish]
appDone: Done. Reports are in {{{dir}}}. Share only the *-diag.json files (and the *-share files, with --share or --report-dir), after reading them; keep the .html reports:
diagnosticsOptionDescription: write a sanitized diagnostics report to share for troubleshooting: what was scanned or skipped, errors, check timings, watch mode status; no code or findings text
redactOptionDescription: extra comma-separated terms to replace in the diagnostics report (company, product or host names); the app name, user name and machine name are always replaced
diagnosticsWritten: Diagnostics written to {{{file}}}: review it before sharing
ingestOptionDescription: also run the traffic checks on a saved capture of the app's traffic: a HAR file (DevTools or proxy export) or Burp Suite "Save items" XML; can be repeated, and works without -i
scopeOptionDescription: a domain the app itself uses (e.g. example.com), for the traffic checks to tell its own hosts from third parties; learned from the traffic when not given; can be repeated
watchTrafficOptionDescription: in watch mode, don't run the traffic checks inside the app (requests, responses and WebSocket messages observed through each window's DevTools protocol connection)
trafficSummary: Traffic: {{http}} HTTP requests and {{ws}} WebSocket messages to {{hosts}} hosts from {{files}} capture file(s)
userDataOptionDescription: review the app's profile folder (its userData: cookies, Local and Session Storage, IndexedDB) for secrets stored in cleartext, read-only; 'auto' finds it by the app's name. Watch mode reviews it after the session
canaryOptionDescription: a unique test password you typed into the app with 'remember me' ticked: its folders (and registry keys on Windows) are searched for it, in plaintext and common encodings; with --watch, what the session wrote is compared too. Can be repeated
searchDirOptionDescription: another folder to search for the --canary password; can be repeated
showSecretsOptionDescription: keep the full values of secrets found at rest in the report (they are already on this machine: don't share such a report)
SECRET_FILE_WRITE_JS_CHECK: A secret is written to a file without encryption
COOKIE_FLAGS_JS_CHECK: A cookie is set in code without its security attributes
HARDCODED_SECRET: A secret is hard-coded in the app package
CODE_SIGNING: Code signature of the packaged executable
installerUnpacked: Unpacked the {{kind}} {{{file}}}: scanning the app inside it
installerNoApp: No Electron app (resources/app.asar or resources/app) was found in the package
nvdOptionDescription: don't look up the Chromium CVEs of the app's Electron version in NVD (slow without an NVD_API_KEY)
findingNotesOptionDescription: a JSON file with your own notes per check or family (explanation, steps, impact, recommendation), shown in the HTML and Word reports; see docs/finding-notes.example.json
suppressOptionDescription: a JSON file of accepted risks by fingerprint, check (TRAFFIC_*) or file, each with a reason and optionally an owner and an expiry date: matching findings are listed apart and leave the scores and --fail-on; see docs/suppressions.example.json
compareOptionDescription: an earlier JSON report of this app: each finding is marked new, unchanged or changed in severity, and what was fixed since is listed
IPC_FILE_ACCESS_JS_CHECK: A file path chosen by a renderer, a navigation or a deep link reaches the file system
IPC_RENDERER_CHANNEL_JS_CHECK: IPC channel used by renderer code
NAVIGATION_REDIRECT_GLOBAL_CHECK: The will-navigate allowlist does not cover server redirects: no will-redirect, did-start-navigation or webRequest handler blocks them
DEVELOPMENT_CODE_JS_CHECK: Development code in the shipped app
DEBUG_LOGGING_JS_CHECK: Verbose logging in the shipped app
SOURCE_MAP_SHIPPED: Source maps ship with the app
watchScreenshotsOptionDescription: in watch mode, save a screenshot of the window as evidence when the marker comes back as live HTML, script is inserted into a page or a navigation carries the marker (to this folder, default ./screenshots; pages can show confidential data)
outputNotWritable: Can't write the report {{{output}}}: the folder {{{dir}}} is not writable ({{{reason}}}). Run from a folder you can write to (e.g. cd to your Documents) or give a full path with -o.
shareOptionDescription: write the findings redacted for sharing (to get help triaging them without handing over the app): names, hosts, user folders, query strings, e-mail and IP addresses, secrets and code are removed; Markdown, or JSON for a .json file. With --app, one per step in the results folder. Review it before sending
shareCodeOptionDescription: include each finding's code in the --share report, with its strings and comments masked
shareWritten: Redacted findings for sharing written to {{{file}}}: review it before sending
reportDirOptionDescription: write this run's reports to their own folder named electronegativity-<UTC date and time>, made inside the given folder (default: the current folder): report.html, report.json, diagnostics.json and shareable-report.md/.json (findings with app, company, user and machine names, domains, addresses and secrets removed, ready to send to a reviewer or an AI agent). With --app, the results folder gets that name
reportDirFailed: Can't create the report folder inside {{{dir}}} ({{{reason}}}). Give a folder you can write to: --report-dir <folder>.
reportDirWithOut: Use either --report-dir (a new folder named electronegativity-<date and time>) or --out (a folder of your choice), not both.
shareAudit: Redaction check: {{{count}}} identifying value(s) that earlier steps missed were replaced in the shareable report
